**This is the phase in which railroad movement (Rule 27\) and truck transport (Rule 23\) are used. The stacking limit (Rule 28\) is checked at the end of this phase.**

### **Stranded Defending Air Units**

Stranded defending air units also land during this phase. These are carrier air units whose aircraft carrier has been damaged or destroyed in combat, or scrambled air units or fighter interceptors whose original territory is now under enemy control. These units are allowed movement of up to one space to find a friendly territory or carrier on which to land. If no landing space can be found, they are lost. This movement occurs before the acting player makes any noncombat movements.

### **Where Units Can Move**

**Land Units.** A land unit can move into any friendly or friendly neutral territory, including territories captured in the current turn. It can’t move into or through a hostile territory or an unfriendly neutral or strict neutral territory. If the United States isn’t at war, it can’t move its units into territories belonging to another Allied power.

This is the only phase in which AAA can move.

**Infantry using railroad movement** (Rule 27\) move 2 spaces instead of 1, subject to all the restrictions above.

**Trucks** may load up to 3 infantry, move up to 2 spaces and unload, all within this phase (Rule 23).

**Air Units.** An air unit must end its move in an eligible landing space. Air units can land in any territory that was friendly (but not friendly neutral) at the start of the current turn.

Only fighters and tactical bombers can land in a sea zone with a friendly carrier present, and a landing spot must be available on the carrier. Additionally:

* A fighter or tactical bomber can land in a sea zone (even a hostile one) adjacent to an industrial complex you own if you will be mobilizing a previously purchased aircraft carrier in that zone during the Mobilize New Units phase.

* In order for a fighter or tactical bomber to land on an existing carrier, both units must END their movement in the same sea zone.

* You must have a carrier move, remain in place, or be mobilized to pick up a fighter or tactical bomber that would end its noncombat movement in a sea zone. You can’t deliberately move an air unit out of range of a potential safe landing space.

Air units that can’t move to an eligible landing space by the end of the Noncombat Move phase are destroyed. A landing territory that is already at its stacking limit is not an eligible landing space.

**Sea Units.** A sea unit can move through any friendly sea zone but can’t move into or through a hostile sea zone. Unlike other sea units, submarines can move through and even into hostile sea zones in this phase; a submarine must end its movement when it enters a sea zone containing one or more enemy destroyers.

**Transports.** Transports can move to friendly coastal territories and load or offload cargo, unless they loaded, moved, offloaded, or were involved in combat during the Combat Move or Conduct Combat phase.

**Aircraft Carriers.** Aircraft carriers can move to sea zones to allow friendly fighters and tactical bombers to land. They must move there, range permitting, if they didn’t move in the Combat Move phase and the friendly sea zone is the only valid landing zone.

### **Movement Restrictions Summary**

| Unit Type | Noncombat Movement Rules |
| :---- | :---- |
| Land Units | Can move into friendly territories, including just-captured ones. Cannot move through hostile or neutral territories. |
| Infantry | \+1 movement from a major industrial complex territory, up to that territory’s IPC value in units (Rule 27\) |
| Trucks | May carry up to 3 infantry, 2 spaces, loading and unloading in this phase only |
| AAA | This is the ONLY phase AAA can move. Follows normal land unit movement rules. |
| Air Units | Must end in a friendly territory or on a carrier. Cannot land in newly captured territories or friendly neutrals. |
| Fighters / Tac Bombers | Can land on carriers in friendly sea zones. Carrier and air unit must end in the same sea zone. |
| Sea Units | Can move through friendly sea zones only. |
| Submarines | CAN move through hostile sea zones. Must stop when entering a sea zone with enemy destroyers. |
| Transports | Can load/offload in friendly coastal territories. Cannot move if already loaded, moved, offloaded, or fought during the combat phases. |
| Aircraft Carriers | Must move to provide a landing zone for fighters/tac bombers if it’s the only valid landing option. |

### **Noncombat Move Checklist**

| Order | Action |
| :---- | :---- |
| 1 | Move stranded defending air units (scrambled fighters, interceptors, carrier air) before any other movement |
| 2 | Land air units that participated in combat (must land in territories friendly at the start of the turn) |
| 3 | Move carriers to pick up fighters/tactical bombers if declared during Combat Move |
| 4 | Move land units (including AAA, trucks and railroad infantry) to reinforce or reposition |
| 5 | Move sea units (transports load/offload, carriers reposition, submarines through hostile zones) |
| 6 | Verify all air units have valid landing zones (destroy any that don’t) |
| 7 | Verify every land territory is within its stacking limit; remove excess units |

### **Special Rules and Restrictions**

**United States Neutral Restrictions.** When the United States is not at war, it cannot move land or air units into territories belonging to another Allied power, move units onto ships belonging to another power, use another power’s naval bases, or end the movement of its sea units in sea zones adjacent to Japanese-controlled territories. Similarly, other Allied powers cannot move land or air units into US territories or onto US ships, or use US naval bases.

**Friendly Neutral Movement.** During Noncombat Move, land units of a power that is at war may move into (but not through) a friendly neutral territory. This converts the territory from neutral status at the end of the phase. The first friendly power to do so places its national control marker on the former friendly neutral territory, and its standing army is immediately activated as units belonging to the new controller.

**Air Units Cannot Land in Newly Captured or Converted Territories.** Air units cannot land in territories captured during this turn, territories converted from friendly neutrals during this turn, or friendly neutral territories at any time.

### **Frequently Forgotten Rules**

* **Stranded air units move FIRST**, before anything else moves.

* **Air cannot land in captured territories**, even though land units can move into them.

* **Carrier must move if promised.**

* **AAA moves ONLY in Noncombat Move.**

* **Transports: one phase or the other.**

* **Submarines can move through hostile zones** (but stop at destroyers).

* **Carrier and air must END in the same zone.**

* **Railroad infantry must start in the major IC territory** — they cannot pick up the bonus by moving into it.

* **Truck cargo must not have moved earlier in the turn**, and cannot move again after unloading.

## **PHASE 6: MOBILIZE NEW UNITS**

Place new units you have purchased on the game board. Only units purchased during your Purchase and Repair Units phase this turn can be mobilized in this phase.

**The stacking limit (Rule 28\) applies. You may not place new units in a land territory beyond its limit.**

### **Placing New Units**

**Land Units.** New land units (infantry, artillery, anti-tank guns, mechanized anti-tank guns, tanks, mechanized infantry, trucks and AAA) can only be mobilized at industrial complexes you control. You can’t place units at newly captured industrial complexes on the turn they are captured.

The number of units that can be mobilized at any one industrial complex is limited by the complex type and by the territory’s IPC value:

* **Minor industrial complex:** up to 3 units per turn

* **Major industrial complex:** up to 10 units per turn (only on originally controlled territories with an IPC value of 3 or more)

The number you can mobilize is also limited to the territory’s IPC value. A major industrial complex built on a territory worth 3 IPCs can mobilize only 3 units per turn, not 10\.

**Air Units.** New air units can be mobilized at any industrial complex you control, subject to the same placement limits as land units. They are placed directly in the territory containing the industrial complex; they do not need an air base.

**Sea Units.** New sea units can only be mobilized at industrial complexes you control on territories adjacent to a sea zone. Place them in any sea zone adjacent to that territory. You can’t place sea units in a sea zone that is or could have become hostile before this phase. Newly mobilized sea units can’t move until your next turn.

### **Facilities**

**Industrial Complexes.** New industrial complexes can only be placed on originally controlled territories with an IPC value of 2 or higher. You can’t place them on captured territories. Only one industrial complex per territory. Minor complexes require an IPC value of 2 or higher; major complexes require 3 or higher.

**Air Bases.** New air bases can be placed on any island or territory you control. An air base allows up to 3 fighters and/or tactical bombers to be scrambled from that territory and increases the movement of air units taking off from it by 1\. Only one air base per territory.

**Naval Bases.** New naval bases can be placed on any island or coastal territory you control. A naval base increases the movement of sea units beginning their movement from an adjacent sea zone by 1 and allows sea units to be repaired there. Only one naval base per territory.

| Facility Type | Mobilization Capacity |
| :---- | :---- |
| Minor Industrial Complex | Up to 3 units per turn (limited by territory IPC value if lower) |
| Major Industrial Complex | Up to 10 units per turn (limited by territory IPC value if lower). Only on originally controlled territories worth 3+ IPCs. Grants railroad movement (Rule 27). |
| Air Base | No mobilization capacity. Provides \+1 movement to air units taking off and allows scrambling of up to 3 fighters/tactical bombers. |
| Naval Base | No mobilization capacity. Provides \+1 movement to sea units beginning movement from an adjacent sea zone and allows repairs. |

### **Special Mobilization Rules**

**Captured Industrial Complexes.** When you capture an enemy industrial complex, you can’t use it to mobilize new units until your next turn. A captured major industrial complex immediately downgrades to a minor one. You can upgrade it back to major on a future turn (if the territory is originally controlled by your power and worth 3+ IPCs) at a cost of 20 IPCs.

**Damaged Facilities.** For each point of damage on an industrial complex, reduce its mobilization capacity by 1\. Damaged air bases and naval bases don’t provide their movement bonuses or other capabilities, but units can still be mobilized at an industrial complex in the same territory.

**Powers Without Capitals.** If your capital is in enemy hands, you can’t mobilize new units anywhere.

**American Lend-Lease.** The free UK Europe fighter and destroyer under Rule 5 are placed during the UK Europe Mobilize New Units phase and do not count against any industrial complex’s capacity.

## **PHASE 7: COLLECT INCOME**

At the end of your turn, collect income based on the total IPC value of all territories you control.

### **Calculating Income**

Add up the IPC values of all territories you control at the end of your turn, including territories you controlled at the start of the game, territories you’ve captured, and friendly neutral territories you’ve moved into. Then collect that many IPCs from the bank.

**National Objectives.** Check your national objectives at the end of your turn. For each objective you meet, collect the bonus IPCs specified, in addition to your regular territorial income.

**Capital Ship Bounty.** Add 1 IPC for each enemy capital ship your power sank this turn (Rule 14).

### **Income Restrictions**

**Capital in Enemy Hands.** If your capital is in enemy hands at the end of your turn, you don’t collect any income, from territories or from national objectives. You retain any IPCs you had in your treasury before your capital was captured, unless the enemy took them.

**Convoy Disruption.** Convoy disruption is resolved separately, in **Phase 8**, immediately after this phase.

### **Income Calculation Worksheet**

| Step | Action |
| :---- | :---- |
| 1 | Add up the IPC values of all territories you control |
| 2 | Check national objectives and add bonus IPCs for each objective you meet |
| 3 | Add 1 IPC per enemy capital ship sunk this turn |
| 4 | If your capital is in enemy hands, collect nothing (income \= 0\) |
| 5 | Collect the final income total from the bank and add it to your treasury |
| 6 | Update your position on the national production chart |
| 7 | Proceed to Phase 8 and resolve convoy disruptions |

## **PHASE 8: CONVOY DISRUPTIONS**

Convoy disruptions are resolved as the final phase of the turn, against the power whose turn it is, immediately after that power has collected its income.

If you control one or more territories with a convoy symbol adjacent to a sea zone, and that sea zone contains enemy submarines or surface warships at the end of your turn, your income is reduced.

For each enemy submarine and each enemy surface warship in that sea zone, roll **one d6** and reduce your income by the die roll value. The maximum reduction for any single sea zone equals the total IPC value of all territories with a convoy symbol adjacent to that sea zone.

*Example: you control two territories adjacent to sea zone 6, with a total value of 5 IPCs. An enemy submarine is in sea zone 6\. You roll a 4\. Your income is reduced by 4 IPCs. If you had rolled a 6, you would lose only 5 IPCs — the maximum for that sea zone.*

**Notes**

* The reduction is taken from the IPCs collected in Phase 7\. If those IPCs have already been added to your treasury, deduct the loss from the treasury.

* A power whose capital is in enemy hands collects no income in Phase 7 and therefore loses nothing in Phase 8\.

* Disruptions of 12 IPCs or more in one turn from originally owned UK Europe territories can award the Axis “London” victory token (Rule 2).

**Why a d6 here.** The convoy roll measures how much income is lost, not whether a hit lands. On a d10 the average loss would nearly double against unchanged caps. It stays a d6 (see Rule 21).

### **Important Reminders**

* **Only units purchased this turn** can be mobilized. You can’t save purchases for future turns.

* **Captured complexes** can’t be used until your NEXT turn, and major complexes downgrade to minor when captured.

* **Damage reduces capacity** by 1 per point.

* **Sea units placement:** sea units must be placed in sea zones adjacent to the industrial complex and can’t be placed in hostile sea zones.

* **Facility limits:** only ONE of each facility type per territory.

* **End-of-turn timing:** income is collected at the END of your turn, after all movement and combat.

* **No income without capital.**

* **Unspent IPCs carry over** (unless your capital is captured).

### **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: Can I mobilize units at a newly captured industrial complex?** A: No. Not until your next turn. A captured major complex also downgrades to a minor one.

**Q: What happens if I can’t mobilize all the units I purchased?** A: You lose the units you can’t place, and the IPCs spent on them. Always check mobilization capacity — and the stacking limit — before purchasing.

**Q: Can I place sea units in a hostile sea zone?** A: No.

**Q: How does damage affect mobilization?** A: Each point of damage reduces mobilization capacity by 1\.

**Q: Do I collect income if my capital is in enemy hands?** A: No — no territorial income and no national objectives, and you can’t purchase or mobilize.

**Q: How does convoy disruption work?** A: In Phase 8, roll one d6 per enemy submarine or surface warship in a sea zone adjacent to your convoy territories. The total reduces the income you just collected, capped at the total IPC value of those convoy territories.

**Q: Can I save IPCs from turn to turn?** A: Yes, unless an enemy captures your capital, in which case they take all your unspent IPCs.

**Q: Does a tactical bomber’s Targeted Attack still trigger AAA fire?** A: Yes. Anti-Aircraft Fire is resolved before combat regardless of what the tactical bomber intends to do.

**Q: Can two tactical bombers name different categories in the same battle?** A: Yes. Each tactical bomber declares independently.

**Q: Do defending aircraft count towards the stacking limit?** A: Yes. Only *attacking* aircraft are exempt.

**Q: Does the ELO IPC pool carry into my treasury if I don’t spend it all?** A: No. Unspent ELO and bid IPCs are lost at the start of the game.

# **The Political Situation**

As the game begins, only France and the United Kingdom are at war with Germany and Italy. In the Pacific, Japan is at war with China, but not yet with the Western Allies. The United States and the Soviet Union are not yet at war with the Axis powers.

## **Germany**

At the beginning of the game, Germany is at war with France and the United Kingdom.

Germany may declare war on the United States or the Soviet Union at the beginning of the Combat Move phase of any of its turns. A state of war between Germany and the Soviet Union will not affect relations between Germany and the United States, and vice versa.

## **Soviet Union**

The Soviet Union begins the game at war with no one. The Molotov-Ribbentrop pact assures that the Soviet Union will remain neutral should Germany go to war in Europe.

The Soviet Union may not declare war on any Axis power before its fourth turn unless an Axis power declares war on it first. However, if London is captured by an Axis power, the Soviet Union may declare war on its following turn.

## **Japan**

Japan begins the game at war with China and no one else.

Japan may declare war on the United Kingdom, UK Pacific, the United States, France and/or the Soviet Union at the beginning of the Combat Move phase of any of its turns, with the following restrictions: if not yet at war with the Western Allies, Japan may not move units into or through China or end the movement of its sea units in sea zones adjacent to any territories containing units belonging to the United States, the United Kingdom or UK Pacific. In addition, Japanese units cannot be moved into Dutch territories unless Japan is at war with the United Kingdom and UK Pacific.

If Japan attacks any territory or sea zone containing units belonging to the United Kingdom or UK Pacific, or moves units into China, then Japan is considered to have declared war on all of these powers. If Japan declares war on any one of the Western Allied powers, it is considered to have declared war on all of them.

If Japan has not declared war on the Western Allies by the Collect Income phase of its third turn, Japan receives a one-time bonus of 10 IPCs at that time.

## **United States**

The United States begins the game at war with no one.

While it remains neutral, in addition to the normal restrictions, the United States may end the movement of its sea units only in sea zones adjacent to US territories, with one exception: US warships (not transports) may conduct long-range patrols into sea zone 102\.

The United States may not declare war on any Axis power unless an Axis power declares war on it first or captures London or any territory in North America, after which it may declare war on any or all Axis powers on its following turn. On turn 3, the United States may declare war on any or all Axis powers at the beginning of the Collect Income phase of that turn if it has not done so already.

## **China**

China begins the game at war with Japan and operates under special restrictions:

* China can only purchase infantry units.

* Chinese infantry must be placed in any Chinese territory controlled by China at the end of the Mobilize New Units phase. China does not need an industrial complex to mobilize units.

* Chinese units can never leave China, with the exception of Burma, Kwangtung and Korea. India, Mongolian and Soviet territories are not part of China.

* Because China has no major industrial complexes, Chinese infantry never gain railroad movement (Rule 27).

## **United Kingdom**

The United Kingdom is divided into two separate economies: United Kingdom Europe and United Kingdom Pacific. Each is managed separately with its own income, purchases and deployments. Both share the same political status — if one is at war, the other is also considered at war.

The United Kingdom is at war with Germany and Italy at the start of the game. It may declare war on Japan at the beginning of the Combat Move phase of any of its turns, subject to Rule 4\.

**United Kingdom Economy Rules.** UK Europe collects income from all original UK territories in Europe and Africa. UK Pacific collects income from all original UK territories in Asia and the Pacific. Each economy makes separate purchases and places units only from its own industrial complexes. The two UK economies may share territories and sea zones freely, but units from one economy cannot use industrial complexes belonging to the other.

## **UK Pacific (formerly ANZAC)**

UK Pacific begins the game neutral and not yet at war with anyone. While not at war, UK Pacific forces cannot leave their original territories and sea zones, and may only be moved for defensive purposes within originally controlled UK Pacific territories.

UK Pacific will be at war with Japan under the same conditions as the United Kingdom, subject to the restriction in Rule 4\.

## **Italy**

At the beginning of the game, Italy is at war with France and the United Kingdom.

Italy may declare war on the United States or the Soviet Union at the beginning of the Combat Move phase of any of its turns.

## **France**

France is at war with Germany and Italy. Either the United States or United Kingdom player will control France and its military units, including the French IPC economy.

If and when the territory France is liberated by the Allies, the player controlling France immediately places their choice of up to 12 IPCs’ worth of any French units on the France territory for free. This can happen only once per game.

# **National Objectives and Bonus Income**

A power collects the indicated bonus IPCs during each of its Collect Income phases if the condition for that bonus has been met, unless otherwise specified.

## **Germany: “Lebensraum”**

**When Germany is not at war with the Soviet Union:**

* 5 IPCs representing wheat and oil from the Soviet Union.

**When Germany is at war with the Soviet Union:**

* 5 IPCs for each of the following territories Germany controls: Novgorod (Leningrad), Volgograd (Stalingrad), Russia (Moscow).

* 5 IPCs if an Axis power controls Caucasus.

**When Germany is at war with the United Kingdom and France:**

* 5 IPCs if at least 1 German land unit is in Axis-controlled Egypt.

* 5 IPCs if Germany controls both Denmark and Norway while Sweden is neither pro-Allies nor Allies-controlled.

* 2 IPCs for each of the following territories Germany controls: Iraq, Persia, Northwest Persia.

* 5 IPCs if at least 5 submarines are on the map — excluding the Baltic sea zones (113, 114, 115\) — during the Collect Income phase, after deploying reinforcements.

## **Soviet Union: “The Great Patriotic War”**

**When the Soviet Union is at war on the European side:**

* 10 IPCs (one time only) the first time the Soviet Union controls Germany (Berlin).

* 10 IPCs if the Soviet Union controls 3 out of the 4 following territories: Finland, Poland, Slovakia/Hungary, Romania.

* 5 IPCs if there are no Allied (non-Soviet) units on any originally controlled Soviet territories.

* 1 Artillery in Archangel if the Soviet Union controls Archangel and the Allies (non-Soviet) control Scotland and Iceland.

* 1 Artillery in Caucasus if the Soviet Union controls Caucasus and the Allies (non-Soviet) control Persia and Northwest Persia.

**When the Soviet Union is at war on the Pacific side:**

* 1 Artillery in Amur if the Soviet Union controls Amur and the Allies control the Aleutian Islands and Alaska.

## **Japan: “The Greater East Asia Co-Prosperity Sphere”**

**When Japan is at war:**

* 5 IPCs if Axis powers control Calcutta.

* One-time bonus of 10 IPCs if Axis powers control all originally Chinese territories ( Kiangsu, Shantung, Hopei, Jehol, Kweichow, Hunan, Kiangsi, Yunnan, Anhwe, Chahar, Suiyuyan, Shensi, Szechwan, Kwangsi, Manchuria \+ the 16th).

* 3 IPCs each for controlling otherwise 0-IPC US, UK Pacific, and UK European, Pacific islands (e.g. Guam, Midway, Fiji).

* 5 IPCs if Axis powers control Burma.

* 5 IPCs if Axis powers control all of: Guam, Midway, Wake Island, Gilbert Islands, Solomon Islands.

* 5 IPCs for each of the following territories Axis powers control: India (Calcutta), New South Wales (Sydney), Hawaiian Islands (Honolulu), Western United States (San Francisco).

* 5 IPCs if Axis powers control all of: Sumatra, Java, Borneo, Celebes.

## **United States: “The Sleeping Giant”**

**When the United States is at war:**

* 10 IPCs if the United States controls both Eastern United States and Central United States.

* 5 IPCs if the United States controls all of: Alaska, Aleutian Islands, Hawaiian Islands, Johnston Island, Line Islands.

* 5 IPCs if the United States controls all of: South Eastern Mexico, Central America, West Indies.

* 5 IPCs if the United States controls the Philippines.

* 5 IPCs if the United States has a land troop in France(Paris).

## **China: “The Flying Tigers”**

**When China is at war:**

* 6 IPCs if the Burma Road is totally open (Allies control India, Burma and Yunnan).

## **United Kingdom Europe**

★ **REPLACES ALL OOB UK EUROPE OBJECTIVES** ★

1. **British Colonies — 5 IPCs.** UK Europe controls all their original territories within the continent of Africa. *Required: Egypt, Anglo-Egyptian Sudan, Union of South Africa, and all other original UK territories in Africa.*

2. **British Commonwealth — 5 IPCs.** UK Europe controls all their original territories outside the continent of Africa. *Required: the UK itself, Scotland, Iceland, Gibraltar, Malta, plus the Canadian territories.*

3. **Mediterranean Theater — 5 IPCs.** There are no Axis surface warships in the Mediterranean Sea (sea zones 92–99).

4. **European Theater — 5 IPCs.** There is at least 1 UK Europe land unit on an originally controlled French territory in Europe.

**Maximum UK Europe bonus: 20 IPCs per turn.**

## **United Kingdom Pacific**

★ **REPLACES ALL OOB UK PACIFIC AND ANZAC OBJECTIVES** ★

*ANZAC has been eliminated in MOD ECR. All former ANZAC territories, units and objectives are now part of UK Pacific.*

1. **Hong Kong — 5 IPCs.** UK Pacific controls Hong Kong. *Must be at war with Japan.*

2. **Malaya — 5 IPCs.** UK Pacific controls Malaya. *Must be at war with Japan.*

3. **Shanghai — 5 IPCs.** The Allies control Shanghai (any Allied power). *Must be at war with Japan.*

4. **Outer Perimeter — 5 IPCs.** UK Pacific has at least 1 land unit on Sumatra, Java, Celebes and/or Dutch New Guinea. *Must be at war with Japan.*

**Maximum UK Pacific bonus: 20 IPCs per turn.**

## **Italy: “Mare Nostrum”**

**When Italy is at war:**

* 5 IPCs if there are no Allied surface warships in the Mediterranean Sea (sea zones 92–99).

* 5 IPCs if Axis powers control at least 3 of: Gibraltar, Southern France, Greece, Egypt.

* 5 IPCs if Axis powers control all of: Morocco, Algeria, Tunisia, Libya, Tobruk, Alexandria.

* 2 IPCs for each of the following territories Italy controls: Iraq, Persia, Northwest Persia.

* 5 IPCs if Axis powers control Cyprus, Crete, Malta, Sardinia and Sicily.

* 5 IPCs if Axis powers control British Somaliland, Italian Somaliland, Ethiopia, Anglo-Egyptian Sudan and Kenya.

# **Appendix A: Open Points for Group Decision**

The five new rules were adopted as written. Applying them to a complete rulebook required a value or a definition in a handful of places where the proposals were silent. Each one below is **live in this edition at the value shown** — change any of them and the rest of the rulebook still works.

| \# | Point | Value used here | Why |
| :---: | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 1 | Infantry attack support by artillery | **Removed at base.** Infantry attacks at 2; artillery boosts infantry *defense* to 3\. Attack support returns only through the Self Propelled Artillery breakthrough | The unit chart lists a Defense Boost for artillery and tanks and no attack support for infantry. Confirmed by breakthrough 1, which grants exactly that attack support |
| 2 | Mech. Infantry “Supported by Artillery” value | **Attacks at 3** when paired 1:1 with artillery | Mirrors the old \+1 support step at the d10 scale |
| 3 | Anti-Tank ability | Hits must be assigned to a Tank, Mech. Infantry or Mech. Anti-Tank Gun if present | The chart names the ability but does not define it |
| 4 | Anti-Aircraft Fire hit number | **1 — not converted upwards** | Group decision. Applies to AAA units, cruiser anti-aircraft fire, facility fire during bombing raids, and the escort/interceptor air battle. Confirmed by the Radar and Jet Fighters breakthroughs, which both raise a base value of 1 |
| 5 | Fighter Interceptor hit number | **1** | Stated explicitly on the unit chart |
| 6 | Tactical bomber “target category” | **A single unit type** (e.g. tanks, battleships, submarines) | Simplest reading of “defender allocates hits according to category chosen by the attacker”. Fixed accuracy is **4** |
| 7 | Bombing damage, convoy disruption and the tech P-3 cost | **Remain d6** | These measure a quantity, not a hit. On a d10 they would nearly double against unchanged caps |
| 8 | Kamikaze strike | **3 or less** | Preserves the OOB 1-in-3 rate |
| 9 | Stacking limit checkpoints | End of Combat Move, Noncombat Move and Mobilize New Units | The proposal gives the limit but not when it is enforced |
| 10 | Stacking limit and allied units | Allied units in a shared territory **count** towards the limit | Otherwise two powers can stack a territory twice over and defeat the rule |
| 11 | Excess units after combat | Owner removes the excess of their choice at the end of Noncombat Move | The proposal does not say what happens when a battle leaves an over-stack |
| 12 | Railroad movement and trucks | May not be combined on the same infantry in the same turn | Otherwise infantry move 4 spaces in a noncombat phase |
| 13 | Artillery Noncombat move (Rule 13\) | **Retained** alongside the new chart | Rule 13 predates the d10 overhaul and was not withdrawn by it |
| 14 | Unspent ELO / bid IPCs | **Lost** at the start of the game | Prevents the balancing pools becoming a turn-1 treasury boost |
| 15 | Aircraft Carrier, Cruiser and Transport costs | 16 / 12 / 7 | Marked as suggested values on the unit chart — the group’s own numbers, not inherited from *A\&A North Africa* |
| 16 | Sea mine detonation | **2 or less** | Converted upwards from 1\. Anti-aircraft fire was deliberately left at 1; if the same reasoning applies to mines, this becomes 1 |
| 17 | Phase 8 convoy disruptions | Resolved **against the power whose turn it is**, deducted from the income just collected | The turn-sequence card reads “Convoy Disruptions against current powers turn”, which could also mean the acting power resolves disruptions it causes against others |

# **Appendix B: Quick Reference Card**

**Dice.** All hit rolls are d10 — roll equal to or under the value. Bombing damage, convoy disruption and the tech P-3 cost are d6. Anti-aircraft fire keeps its out-of-box hit number of 1\.

**Turn sequence.** 1 Research and Development · 2 Purchase and Repair · 3 Combat Move · 4 Conduct Combat · 5 Noncombat Move · 6 Mobilize New Units · 7 Collect Income · 8 Convoy Disruptions.

**Combat sequence.** Battle strip → Anti-Aircraft Fire and Interceptor shots → Submarine Surprise Strike → Attacker fires → Defender fires → Remove casualties → Press or retreat → Conclude.

**Key hit numbers.**

| Roll | Hits on |
| :---- | :---- |
| Anti-Aircraft Fire (AAA ×3, Cruiser ×2) | 1 |
| Fighter Interceptor | 1 |
| Attacking submarine Surprise Strike | 4 or less |
| Defending submarine Surprise Strike | 2 or less |
| Tactical bomber Targeted Attack | 4 or less |
| Battleship bombardment | 7 or less |
| Cruiser bombardment | 5 or less |
| Kamikaze | 3 or less |
| Facility antiaircraft fire vs bombers | 1 |
| Air battle (escorts vs interceptors) | 1 |
| Sea mine | 2 or less |
| Strategic bomber vs undefended transport | 7 or less |
| Technology discovery roll at H | 3 or less |

**Combined arms.**

| Combination | Effect |
| :---- | :---- |
| Infantry \+ Artillery (defending) | Up to 2 Infantry per Artillery defend @ 3 |
| Infantry \+ Tank (defending) | Up to 2 Infantry per Tank defend @ 3 |
| Mech. Infantry \+ Artillery | Mech. Infantry attacks @ 3 |
| Mech. Infantry \+ Tank | Mech. Infantry can blitz |
| Artillery \+ Mech. Infantry | Artillery moves 2 in Noncombat Move |
| Plane \+ Destroyer | Plane can hit submarines |

**Stacking limit.** 10 \+ territory IPC value. Exempt: AAA, Trucks, attacking aircraft.

**Railroad movement.** Infantry starting in a major industrial complex territory move 2 in Noncombat Move, up to that territory’s IPC value in units.

# **Appendix C: Research and Development — Breakthrough Charts**

These are the eleven technologies available through the Technology Research System (Rule 20). Research one at a time, chosen secretly when you enter the track. The research procedure — the 4-IPC entry, the P-1 and P-2 advancement costs, the P-3 roll and the discovery dice at H — is set out in full in **Rule 20**.

## **How Breakthroughs Convert to d10**

The breakthrough cards were written for the six-sided system, so a card that reads “increases to 3, up from 2” is describing a d6 value that no longer exists.

**The conversion rule: a breakthrough that raises a die value adds \+2 to that unit’s d10 value. Ignore the number printed on the card.**

*Example: Super Submarines reads “Submarine attack increases to 3, up from 2.” Under d10 the submarine attacks at 4, so the breakthrough takes it to **6** — not to 3\.*

Breakthroughs that do not change a die value — extra dice, extra capacity, extra range — carry across exactly as printed.

## **Breakthrough Chart 1**

| \# | Technology | P-1 | P-2 | P-3 |
| :---: | :---- | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| 1 | Self Propelled Artillery | 4 | 4 | ROLL |
| 2 | Super Battleships | 4 | 4 | ROLL |
| 3 | Heavy Bombers | 4 | 4 | ROLL |
| 4 | Super Carriers | 4 | 4 | ROLL |
| 5 | Heavy Tanks | 4 | 4 | ROLL |
| 6 | Improved Transports | 4 | 4 | ROLL |

**1 — Self Propelled Artillery**

*As printed:* Artillery now supports 2 Infantry or Mechanized units; in addition, moves 2, up from 1\.

*Under d10:* Each artillery may support **up to 2 Infantry and/or Mechanized Infantry when attacking**, raising each supported unit’s attack from **2 to 3**. In addition, artillery **Move goes from 1 to 2** in all phases.

This is an attacking bonus and is in addition to the artillery’s base Defense Boost (Rule 24), which is unaffected. It also replaces the base 1:1 “Supported by Artillery” pairing for mechanized infantry — one artillery now supports two units instead of one, and infantry as well as mech infantry.

**2 — Super Battleships**

*As printed:* Battleships now roll 2 dice on attacks and bombardments.

*Under d10:* Unchanged. Each battleship rolls two dice, each hitting on 7 or less, in combat and in naval bombardment.

**3 — Heavy Bombers**

*As printed:* Bombers now roll 2 dice on attacks and bombing raids.

*Under d10:* Unchanged. Each strategic bomber rolls two attack dice, each hitting on 7 or less. On a bombing raid it rolls two d6 damage dice, each with the \+2 strategic bomber modifier.

**4 — Super Carriers**

*As printed:* Carriers now support 3 planes.

*Under d10:* Unchanged. Each aircraft carrier carries 3 fighters and/or tactical bombers instead of 2\.

**5 — Heavy Tanks**

*As printed:* Tanks now defend at 4 (up from 3).

*Under d10:* Tanks defend at **7** (5 \+ 2). Attack is unaffected.

**6 — Improved Transports**

*As printed:* Naval transports can now carry any 2 ground units, plus 1 Infantry.

*Under d10:* Unchanged. A transport carries any 2 land units plus 1 additional infantry. Trucks and Anti-Aircraft Artillery count as ground units for this purpose.

## **Breakthrough Chart 2**

| \# | Technology | P-1 | P-2 | P-3 |
| :---: | :---- | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| 7 | Super Submarines | 4 | 4 | ROLL |
| 8 | Jet Fighters | 4 | 4 | ROLL |
| 9 | Improved Shipyards | 4 | 4 | ROLL |
| 10 | Radar | 4 | 4 | ROLL |
| 11 | Long Range Aircraft | 4 | 4 | ROLL |

**7 — Super Submarines**

*As printed:* Submarine attack increases to 3, up from 2\.

*Under d10:* Submarines attack at **6** (4 \+ 2). This applies to the Surprise Strike roll as well as to normal attack rolls. Defense is unaffected.

**8 — Jet Fighters**

*As printed:* Fighter attack increases to 4; escorting and intercepting fighter hits are increased to 2\.

*Under d10:* Fighters attack at **6** (4 \+ 2). In the escort/interceptor air battle they hit on **3** (1 \+ 2). The fighter’s own Interceptor ability (Rule 24\) likewise hits on **3** instead of 1\. Defense is unaffected.

**9 — Improved Shipyards**

*As printed:* See “Unit Statistics” chart for Improved Shipyard unit costs.

*Under d10:* Naval unit costs are reduced to the values below for the rest of the game. All other statistics are unchanged.

| Sea Unit | Normal Cost | Improved Shipyards |
| :---- | :---: | :---: |
| Submarine | 6 | **5** |
| Transport | 7 | **5** |
| Destroyer | 8 | **7** |
| Cruiser | 12 | **8** |
| Aircraft Carrier | 16 | **13** |
| Battleship | 20 | **16** |

**10 — Radar**

*As printed:* Anti-Aircraft units and Facility fire is increased to 2; Air Bases can scramble unlimited planes, up from 3\.

*Under d10:* Anti-Aircraft Artillery, cruiser anti-aircraft fire and facility antiaircraft fire all hit on **3** instead of 1 (1 \+ 2). Air bases may scramble an unlimited number of fighters and tactical bombers instead of 3\.

**11 — Long Range Aircraft**

*As printed:* All air unit range is increased by two spaces.

*Under d10:* Unchanged. Fighters and tactical bombers move 6, strategic bombers move 8 — each still \+1 more when taking off from an operative air base.

# **Credits and Version History**

MOD ECR is based on Out-of-Box Axis & Allies Global 1940 Second Edition rules with modifications inspired by competitive tournament play and community house rules. Unit stats in Section C are based on *Axis & Allies North Africa*, with modifications.

**Version History**

* **v3.0 — August 2026:** Conversion to the d10 system with a full unit stat overhaul; new units (Anti-Tank Gun, Mechanized Anti-Tank Gun, Truck); tactical bomber Targeted Attack at fixed accuracy 4; ELO game balancing; railroad movement for infantry; land area stacking limit; Research and Development breakthrough charts added as Appendix C, with the R\&D procedure rewritten to the breakthrough card. Turn sequence expanded to eight phases, splitting Research and Development and Convoy Disruptions into phases of their own. All die references in Parts I and II converted, except anti-aircraft fire, which stays at 1\.

* **v2.0 — January 2026:** Complete edition merging core and advanced rules.

* **v1.0 — January 2026:** Core competitive modifications.
